title: Sharp Buncher Treatment Effect Bounds under Stochastic Increasingness and Bi-Log-Concavity at Kinks
banked_reason: D0.5 math review passed, but the general referee found tier=incremental, meets_floor=false, and paper_score_ceiling 6.1 < 7.4; the exact general finite-M endpoint remains genuinely open.
gap_reasons: The note proves a sharp pointwise expansion as M approaches zero, but at general positive M it supplies only a separate-cut outer envelope; simultaneous feasibility and endpoint attainment remain open.
The exact identified interval is proved only for fixed uniform margins and M≤1, so it does not settle the advertised general completion problem.
paper_score_ceiling 6.1 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'.
proof_attempt_summary: The run audited the anchored bi-log-concave completion model, repaired its shrinking-width definition, and established sound local and fixed-uniform results. It could not jointly optimize the two hidden marginal segments and a single ordered bidirectionally-SI coupling at fixed positive M; certified convergence to the general endpoint and endpoint attainment remain the original unsolved kernel, so the field-floor run terminated at incremental.
tldr: Under ordered choices, mutual stochastic increasingness, shrinking-neighborhood effect widths, anchored bi-log-concave hidden margins, and the full observed kink law, the upper buncher ATE has a sharp quadratic small-width expansion with an explicit coefficient. The note also gives a separate-cut finite-width outer envelope, proves the entire fixed-uniform identified interval for 0≤M≤1, and proves interval structure for the general identified set. Simultaneous-window compatibility and the exact general positive-width endpoint and attainment rule remain open.
gap: The observed law fixes only visible marginal tails and bunching mass. Existing BLC and SI bounds do not characterize their joint finite-width completion, and the law-invariant two-cut width restriction can make separate extrema incompatible.
fill: Derive an exact finite-M endpoint and inclusion criterion, or a certified continuum inner/outer procedure at the original width; establish the proposed quadratic local boundary behavior and identify when cut envelopes are jointly feasible.
